visual_events.label: Mason scoops and spreads mortar Bed over a row of bricks laid on edge
visual_events.description: In a static medium-wide shot on sandy ground under trees, the mason (ent_mason) bends over a low red-brick wall section (ent_brick_wall) where bricks are positioned on their narrow edge. At 0.0s–2.0s he spreads and levels grey mortar with a trowel (ent_trowel) along a short front row of five upright header/stretcher bricks. He scoops additional wet grey mortar from the metal pan (ent_mortar_pan) at lower right around 2.1s–3.7s, 5.1s–6.5s, and 8.9s–10.5s, depositing and smoothing each trowel load onto the top of that brick-on-edge row while tucking stray mortar along the sides. Between 10.6s and 11.4s a second person (ent_helper) briefly steps in at the right frame edge, sets down a red brick near the pan, and exits right. From 11.0s to 14.4s the mason finishes smoothing and shaping the mortar bed with the trowel.
visual_events.context_result: A continuous, smoothed bed of wet grey mortar rests on top of the lower row of bricks laid on edge, ready to receive the next brick.
visual_events.camera_framing: Static tripod medium-wide eye-level/slightly low-angle shot; full body of bent mason stays in frame during mortar work.
visual_events.uncertainty: Between 10.6s and 11.4s a second person's arm and leg intrude at the extreme right edge of the frame.

visual_events.label: Mason picks up a red brick and chips/trims it with the trowel
visual_events.description: At 14.4s the mason (ent_mason) reaches down with his left hand to pick up a red brick from the ground beside the wall, straightening his posture at 15.6s so that his head rises above the top edge of the frame. Holding the brick in his left hand and the trowel (ent_trowel) in his right, he inspects the brick, flips it, and from 17.0s to 19.2s strikes the brick face/edge repeatedly with the side of the metal trowel, knocking small red brick fragments and dust downward toward the ground as the clip ends.

additional_analysis.attempts: This 19.2s source clip consists of one continuous, uncut camera take showing two successive masonry stages on the same low brick-on-edge wall rather than repeated camera takes. Within the first stage (ve_01_mortar_spreading, 0.0s–14.4s), the mason performs three repeated physical mortar-scooping and spreading cycles from the metal pan onto the same row of upright bricks: cycle 1 is already underway at 0.0s–2.0s (spreading existing mortar), followed by scoop and spread cycle 2 at 2.1s–5.0s, scoop and spread cycle 3 at 5.1s–8.8s, and scoop and final smoothing cycle 4 at 8.9s–14.4s (during which a helper briefly intrudes at the right frame edge at 10.6s–11.4s). At 14.4s–19.2s the clip transitions to a new process stage (ve_02_brick_pickup_and_trimming), where the mason picks up a brick and chips/trims it with his trowel until the recording cuts off at 19.2s.
additional_analysis.crop_guidance: For standard landscape output, the full frame from 0.0s to 10.4s is well composed, keeping the bent mason (ent_mason), trowel (ent_trowel), mortar pan (ent_mortar_pan), and L-shaped brick-on-edge wall (ent_brick_wall) cleanly inside the center and lower thirds. If using the span across 10.6s–11.4s (ve_01_mortar_spreading), a slight zoom/crop excluding the rightmost ~10–12% of the frame would remove the brief intrusion of the second person's arm and leg (ent_helper) at the right edge while still preserving part of the mortar pan and all of the mason's trowel work. Conversely, from 15.6s to 19.2s (ve_02_brick_pickup_and_trimming), the mason stands upright and his head rises out of the top of the frame; no crop can restore his missing head, though a tighter medium/close crop focused on the lower-center region (hands, trowel, brick being chipped, and top of the brick wall) could salvage the brick-trimming action if needed. This is approximate framing guidance, not verified pixel clearance.

evidence_limits.limitation: Visual inspection of the red bricks and mortar work cannot establish the bricks' crushing strength (20, 35, or 75 kg/cm²), whether they are wire-cut or kiln-burnt to a specific standard, or the 25% material reduction figure cited in the script.
